title: EmberCore marketplace VPC & KMS onboarding sync
summary: Kickoff deep-dive for EmberCore's Azure marketplace listing plus private VPC connectivity and KMS onboarding. Reviewed listing artifact requirements, network/firewall patterns, entitlement & private offer flows, and audit/KMS vault integration. Agreed to run an integration test in Redwood staging, provide manifest and sample ARM templates, and schedule a 2-hour POC kickoff next week.
topics: Marketplace listing manifest and SKU mapping
Private offers vs SaaS marketplace entitlements
VPC peering / private endpoint patterns and firewall rules
KMS/HSM integration for model keys and customer encryption
action_items: Owner: EmberCore (Priya) | Item: Share current ARM template and listing manifest draft | Due: 2026-07-01
Owner: Redwood (Ravi) | Item: Provide staged sample ARM + Terraform snippets and a manifest checklist for Azure Marketplace listing | Due: 2026-06-29
Owner: EmberCore (Tomás) | Item: Confirm KMS provider and account details for test vault (Azure Key Vault vs. HSM) | Due: 2026-06-30
Owner: Redwood (Alex) | Item: Create Redwood staging workspace and invite EmberCore testers, enable VPC test routing rules | Due: 2026-07-02
next_steps: Redwood to provision staging tenant and send invite link
EmberCore to upload manifest draft and ARM template to shared drive
Schedule 2-hour POC kickoff (end-to-end test with KMS and private endpoint) for next week
Exchange security questionnaire and SOC-2 evidence relevant to listing
transcript:
Header: 2026-06-25 14:00 PT | Duration: 58m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Singh (Redwood SE), Dana Morales (EmberCore Head Partnerships), Priya Iyer (EmberCore Platform), Tomás Ortega (EmberCore Security), Leo Park (EmberCore DevOps)

Summary (auto): high-level and technical alignment on Azure marketplace listing + private VPC and KMS. Next: staged POC, manifest and templates shared, security docs.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone—thanks for joining. quick agenda: listing artifacts, network, kms, and POC plan. If we get through the manifest and the network pattern we should be able to sign off on a staging run.
[00:18] Dana Morales: Yeah, thank you. we pulled the right people who own the listing and platform. Priya will share the manifest later. Tomás is here for security questions.
[00:30] Priya Iyer: hi all. our goal is to get the EmberCore offer live in marketplace with a private entitle flow for our enterprise customers. we need a path for private endpoints into Redwood and we must ensure customer keys remain in our KMS.
[00:47] Ravi Singh: great, we saw similar patterns with other partners—Redwood supports private endpoints and can route through a VPC peering or private link pattern depending on cloud. For Azure specifically we usually recommend private endpoint with a restricted NSG and an internal DNS override so the SDK hits the private IP.
[01:10] Tomás Ortega: can you say more about KMS? our compliance people, we use Azure Key Vault but we also have a BYOK HSM in some contracts. we need assurance that model secret material, or rather the tokens/keys used to fetch model weights or encryption keys, never leave the vault unencrypted.
[01:32] Ravi Singh: yeah. in Redwood private deployments we integrate with customer KMS via key wrapping; Redwood never stores plaintext keys. For hosted listings we can offer a private deployment option where the control plane is in Redwood but the key wraps happen in the customer KMS. There may be slight differences in the OAuth handshake for the catalog listing—I'll go over that.
[01:56] Alex Chen: small caveat—when customers choose a marketplace private offer versus the public SaaS offer the provisioning flow changes. for private offers we hand off an entitlement token that your system redeems. that token is how we gate access to the dedicated tenant.
[02:20] Dana Morales: Right, and we have enterprise customers who require audit logs written to their logging sink. can we stream per-request logs into their workspace or do we give them an export?
[02:35] Ravi Singh: we support both. for Redwood Dedicated or Private we can push audit events to your event hub or via forwarder. for hosted we provide secure audit exports. there's a config knob to decide retention and fields—Tomás, you'll like that because we can exclude PII.
[02:51] Tomás Ortega: good. also need SSO/SAML mapping for RBAC in your console for our internal admins.
[03:02] Alex Chen: yep SAML, SCIM provisioning—we have a guide. we'll share the quickstart.
[03:12] Leo Park: scratching in on networking—firewall side: do you need specific source IP ranges from the marketplace provisioning system or from the runtime nodes? because our infra team blocks ranges aggressively.
[03:28] Ravi Singh: good question. for the marketplace tile the initial handshake comes from the marketplace provisioning endpoints which are public, but the runtime egress will come from our regional egress list. for private endpoint patterns the traffic will come over the private link so it's your internal prefix. we will send a short list of IP ranges and the private endpoint DNS overrides.
[03:52] Dana Morales: timeline—we were hoping to be in a pilot with 2 customers by mid-July. is that realistic?
[04:01] Alex Chen: yes if we get manifest and KMS details this week we can target a POC kickoff next week and an internal pilot mid-July. need to confirm how quickly Azure Marketplace listing gating takes; sometimes private offers take longer for marketplace validation.
[04:22] Priya Iyer: walking through the manifest: we have SKU mapping that corresponds to EmberCore's tiers—dev, team, enterprise—how do you map that to Redwood model variants or instance sizes?
[04:38] Ravi Singh: we usually map SKUs to model profiles—dev maps to small instances (gpt-small-ish quantized), team to medium, enterprise to dedicated capacity or larger instance types. for marketplace metering we emit dimensioned usage events back to the marketplace meter so charges pass through to the customer's subscription.
[05:00] Tomás Ortega: any specifics on metering—do you rely on Azure Metering API or do you send aggregated records?
[05:09] Ravi Singh: we integrate with the Marketplace metering service and can support both per-call and aggregated billing. per-call metering requires low-latency reporting but we've implemented batching and reconciliation in Redwood Optimize to avoid mismatches.
[05:28] Alex Chen: quick aside, competitor note: CloudVendorX requires a custom gateway; our approach avoids another hop which helps latency.
[05:38] Dana Morales: ok, let's talk about the POC plan. what does a 2-week POC look like?
[05:46] Ravi Singh: step 1: share manifest + ARM/Terraform. step 2: Redwood stages a tenant and we wire KMS keys and private endpoint. step 3: run end-to-end test with a sample subscription and a private entitle. step 4: run perf smoke tests to validate latency and throughput at your target sizes.
[06:10] Priya Iyer: for the perf test can you run a KV cache simulation? our use-case has long prompt prefixes so cache behavior matters.
[06:22] Ravi Singh: yes we can instrument the KV cache hit rate and share per-token cost numbers. in staging we'll enable prefix caching and measure token cost and tail latencies.
[06:35] Tomás Ortega: compliance asks—SOC 2 / ISO artifacts. will you share those ahead of the POC?
[06:45] Alex Chen: yes we'll attach the SOC 2 and ISO summary; for anything deeper we can do a security questionnaire. we'll also share a redacted runbook for incident response.
[06:58] [background murmur, brief crosstalk]
[07:12] Dana Morales: small policy question: can customers force keys to rotate without redeploying models?
[07:20] Ravi Singh: our key wrapping supports rotation. as long as the KMS supports wrap/unwrap semantics we can rotate the customer wrapping key; the runtime will pick up new wraps with zero-downtime if you follow the rotation schedule. there are edge cases with persistent caches where you'll want to flush cached sessions.
[07:40] Leo Park: does Redwood's agent require outbound internet for telemetry or can that go via private link into our logging stack?
[07:50] Ravi Singh: telemetry can be forwarded via private link into your logging sink. we can also disable telemetry in high-security configs and rely on customer-run probes.
[08:05] Alex Chen: ok let's surface the concrete checklist we need to collect from EmberCore: manifest, ARM/Terraform, KMS account info + service principal, list of test subscriptions, and a security contact.
[08:22] Priya Iyer: we have those, will collate. For service principal we need a least-priv role; can you send the specific IAM permissions?
[08:32] Ravi Singh: yes we'll send a short permissions doc. normally it's read/list on network resources, permission to create private endpoint link, and a key unwrap permission for the vault.
[08:47] Dana Morales: question from procurement—how does the subscription handoff work if the customer wants to be billed through their Azure invoice?
[08:58] Alex Chen: for marketplace public SaaS we bill through the Marketplace. for private offers we tie the entitlement to your subscription so charges flow through their invoice. if you need a reseller flow there's an extra onboarding step.
[09:14] Tomás Ortega: are there any known incompatibilities with our existing ingress WAF?
[09:20] Ravi Singh: not typically. with private endpoints the WAF sits in front of the customer's front-door; the traffic hitting Redwood is from the private IP space. we will do a connectivity test during POC and surface any rule adjustments.
[09:38] [15m mark omitted for brevity, discussion continues on more detailed steps]
[15:02] Alex Chen: I'll capture next steps and action items. brief recap: Redwood provides manifest checklist, sample templates, staging tenant. EmberCore provides manifest, KMS details, and test subscriptions. schedule POC kickoff.
[15:22] Dana Morales: sounds good. can we get a time for that 2-hour session? next Thu morning PT works for our engineers.
[15:30] Alex Chen: I'll propose two slots and include Ravi.
[15:36] Priya Iyer: one more quick: when you say you stream audit logs, what schema? we need event id, request id, user id, and model id.
[15:48] Ravi Singh: we have a standard audit schema; we'll share a sample JSON schema. we can add fields as needed.
[16:00] Tomás Ortega: and can we redact prompts in logs? some customers consider prompts sensitive.
[16:08] Ravi Singh: yes redaction and PII filters are configurable; we can mask prompt content and retain only tokens counts and metrics.
[16:20] Dana Morales: ok great. anything else?
[16:25] Alex Chen: no, that's it. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with docs and invite for POC kickoff.
[16:34] [end of recording notes]
